Cultural Diversity

Cultural diversity — cultural competence, beliefs affecting health, and culturally sensitive care.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Define cultural competence
  • Describe how culture affects health beliefs
  • Explain culturally sensitive nursing care

In simple words

Cultural diversity means people differ in culture, religion, language, food and beliefs. Culturally competent care respects these differences and adapts care to each patient’s culture.

Culture affects health beliefs, diet, modesty, family roles, pain expression and decision-making.

Culturally sensitive care

  • Ask about cultural and religious beliefs.
  • Respect dietary restrictions (fasting, vegetarian, halal, kosher).
  • Respect modesty — offer same-gender care when possible.
  • Use interpreters when language differs; do not use children.
  • Involve the family if the patient’s culture makes decisions as a family.

Common cultural effects on health

Area Cultural effect
Diet Fasting, food restrictions, vegetarianism
Modesty Same-gender preference, covering the body
Decision-making Individual or family-based
Pain Open expression or silent endurance
Illness beliefs Natural, supernatural or biomedical causes

🔴 Ask, don’t assume

Ask about cultural and religious beliefs — do not assume. Respect dietary, modesty and family preferences.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Admission assessment — ask about culture, religion, language and food preferences.
  • Diet — arrange culturally appropriate meals; respect fasting.
  • Modesty — offer same-gender caregivers for intimate care.
  • Communication — use trained interpreters; translate key documents.
  • Family involvement — ask who makes decisions and involve them.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Cultural competence respects and adapts care to each patient’s culture.
  2. Culture affects diet, modesty, family roles, pain expression and decisions.
  3. Respect dietary restrictions (fasting, vegetarian, halal, kosher).
  4. Use trained interpreters when language differs — not children.
  5. Ask who makes decisions; involve the family if culturally expected.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Pain expression varies by culture — some express openly, some silently.
  2. Offer same-gender caregivers for intimate care.
  3. Avoid stereotypes; treat each patient as an individual.
  4. Illness beliefs vary — natural, supernatural or biomedical.

📌 Memory trick

Cultural care: “A-R-A” — Ask, Respect, Adapt.

60-second revision

  • Cultural diversity = differences in culture, religion, language, beliefs.
  • Culturally competent care respects and adapts to culture.
  • Culture affects diet, modesty, family roles, pain, decisions.
  • Use interpreters; respect fasting and modesty.
  • Ask who makes decisions; involve family.

Test yourself

Cultural competence means:

Answer: B. Cultural competence means respecting and adapting care to each patient’s culture.

When a patient’s language differs, the nurse should:

Answer: B. Use a trained interpreter for accurate, confidential communication.

Modesty in care means:

Answer: B. Respect modesty — offer same-gender caregivers for intimate care.

Pain expression:

Answer: B. Pain expression varies — some cultures express openly, some endure silently.

Family involvement in decisions:

Answer: B. Ask the patient who should be involved; this depends on culture and preference.
